newsitem.title: UK: Chinese barman prepares for Beijing's first pub.
newsitem.headline: Chinese barman prepares for Beijing's first pub.

text.p: A Chinese barman who is to work from next February in what is claimed to be the first authentic British pub in Beijing came to the end of a training stint in London on Friday and seemed well pleased with his career choice.
"I love it, I love this atmosphere," Ping Yuan said, between pulling pints at the Horniman pub in one of London's plusher riverside developments near London Bridge.

The besuited, well-heeled customers there might not be typical of the average London drinker but should prepare him for opening night in Beijing -- the new pub is just around the corner from the British embassy.
The "John Bull Pub" will be the 60th opened around the world, according to Simon Keep, who is Overseas Development Manager for Allied Domecq Retailing Ltd,, which owns the chain.
There are two in Moscow, several more in eastern Europe and others in the Far East and Scandinavia. All serve a range of British beers plus standard British fare like fish and chips.
However, Keep said the new pub did not aim to cater for the British expatriate alone.
"Beijing is a fast-changing city. The people are more aspirational, they watch television and see Western images and are interested by the Western life-style," he said.
The Beijing pub will have an English manager, and Ping -- apparently known as Bob, a testimony to the British inability to master even the simplest of foreign names -- will be his deputy.

Sadly, his new-found cellar skills will not be fully tested in Beijing. The John Bull pub will serve Allied's keg beers, but not the cask ales preferred by the more discerning British beer drinker. They would not survive the journey, Keep said.
